participantInstructions: This is a team decision-making event that requires two (2) participants. The event is presented to the participant team through its reading of the 21st Century Skills, the Performance Indicators, and the Case Study Situation. The participant team has thirty (30) minutes to review the case study situation, develop a solution, and prepare its presentation. The participant team then has fifteen (15) minutes to present its recommendation to the judge and respond to the judge's questions. Both members of the participant team must participate in the presentation and in answering the judge's questions. All notes and materials are turned in to the judge at the end of the presentation.
situation:
You are the operations manager and the customer relations manager, the participant team, at COBALT CREST MOVING & STORAGE, a regional moving and storage company. The general manager (judge) has asked the participant team to meet to work through a scheduling conflict that has surfaced across two commitments the company has already made to its customers. The general manager (judge) is looking to the participant team for one clear, defensible recommendation before either commitment moves forward this week.

Cobalt Crest formed six months ago when Cobalt Relocation Services merged with Crest Storage Solutions, combining two regional crews under one name and one brand promise: "On time, every move, every time," printed on every truck and every quote the company sends. Since the merger, only one crew holds certification recognized by both companies' insurance carriers to handle high-value commercial relocations; the remaining crews are still completing the cross-training required before they can be assigned to jobs of that size.

Last month, a subcontractor inherited from Crest's roster handled the relocation of Whitfield Manufacturing's headquarters while the certified crew was committed elsewhere. The subcontractor arrived a day late and damaged several display cases during the move. Whitfield's plant manager, a client of ten years, told the general manager (judge) directly that the delay embarrassed him in front of his own leadership team. Cobalt Crest apologized and promised that its certified crew, not another subcontractor, would personally handle Whitfield's remaining satellite-office move next week.

This week, Highline Retail Group offered Cobalt Crest an exclusive three-year contract to relocate twelve store locations, on the condition that the certified crew begin the first phase immediately, the same week already promised to Whitfield. No other crew is certified to handle either job, and Highline has indicated that it is also in talks with a competing moving company. Cobalt Crest had built its planned regional promotional campaign, announcing expanded capacity after the merger, around the credibility of landing a contract this size.

The general manager (judge) wants the participant team to recommend which commitment the certified crew should honor this week, and how the company should handle the relationship that does not receive the crew in a way that keeps its trust intact. The general manager (judge) also wants a recommendation for what Cobalt Crest should communicate to whichever party is affected, and when that message should be delivered.

The general manager (judge) will greet the participant team at the start of the meeting and ask to hear its recommendation for handling both commitments. The general manager (judge) will listen to the full presentation before asking any follow-up questions, and will give the participant team a chance to respond to each one fully. Once those questions are finished, the general manager (judge) will thank the participant team for its work and close the meeting.
judgeCharacterization:

judgeQuestions: What would you tell Whitfield Manufacturing before you make your final call?
